findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'multi-parent' claim with sync._union_merge's actual TWO-parent `git merge` (sync.py:182-190): specify how the doctor folds N (≥3) divergent heads (octopus `git merge h1 h2 …` vs. iterated pairwise merges) and state explicitly which behavior the shared primitive preserves for sync vs. adds for the doctor.

search for 'allow-unrelated-histories' confirms the only extra flag is the unrelated-histories case, still a two-parent merge
sync's merge is thus not 'multi-parent' in the N-head sense the doctor needs
findings.finding: The plan asserts sync._union_merge is a 'lossless multi-parent git merge' and that a shared primitive 'both call' can fold 'all fetched heads into HEAD' as 'a single multi-parent merge commit T' with 'the same lossless semantics sync._union_merge uses.' The code (src/rebar/_store/sync.py:171-197) shows _union_merge runs `git merge <single merge_target>`, producing a strictly TWO-parent commit; it has no N-way/octopus merge path. sync merges HEAD + exactly one remote target, whereas the doctor must fold N divergent bundle heads. The 'multi-parent, all-heads, same primitive both call' framing overstates the existing behavior and leaves the N-head fold mechanism (octopus vs. iterated pairwise merges) unspecified.
findings.location: Approach step 4 & Scope (sync.py factoring); AC 'sync.py merge-primitive extraction is behavior-preserving'
scenarios: A ref with THREE or more divergent bundles: sync's two-parent primitive cannot fold all heads in one commit, so the doctor must iterate — undocumented
Extraction that keeps sync's two-parent shape while claiming it serves the N-head doctor may under-deliver the primitive the doctor depends on
findings.suggested_fix: State that sync._union_merge is a two-parent merge and that the extracted primitive either (a) accepts a list of targets and performs an octopus/iterated fold, with sync passing a single-element list (preserving its exact two-parent behavior), or (b) the doctor loops the primitive pairwise across the N fetched scratch refs. Drop the 'multi-parent' characterization of the current sync code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether the doctor folds N heads via SEQUENTIAL 2-parent merges (reusing `_union_merge` per fetched head) or a true octopus merge, and reconcile that with the 'one shared primitive, behaviour-preserving for sync' claim (octopus and 2-parent merge have different conflict semantics).
evidence: Plan: 'Create a single multi-parent merge commit T folding all fetched heads into HEAD with the shared primitive (the same lossless semantics sync._union_merge uses, factored into one primitive both call)'
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:171-196 `_union_merge` runs one `git merge <merge_target>` (a single 2-parent merge), not an N-way octopus
git octopus merge (`git merge A B C`) fails outright on any conflicting merge and cannot use a conflict-resolution path
findings.finding: The plan claims the doctor 'folds all fetched heads into HEAD with the shared primitive (the same lossless semantics sync._union_merge uses)' and calls this 'behaviour-preserving for sync', but sync._union_merge performs a single 2-parent `git merge` of one target ref, whereas folding N bundle heads into one commit T is an octopus (N-parent) merge with materially different semantics — octopus git merge aborts on ANY non-trivial conflict and cannot apply a resolution strategy. For N>2 bundles the 'one primitive both call' factoring is not straightforwardly correct or behaviour-preserving.
findings.location: Approach step 4 / Scope (sync.py extraction) / AC line 'sync.py merge-primitive extraction is behavior-preserving'
scenarios: Three or more divergent bundles exist for the ref, each carrying unique events
Any pair of the N heads has a real content overlap that a 2-parent merge would resolve but octopus refuses
findings.suggested_fix: State that the doctor iterates the shared 2-parent `_union_merge` primitive once per fetched head (merging them into HEAD one at a time), so the extracted primitive is byte-for-byte what sync calls; reserve 'multi-parent' wording for the cumulative result, not a single octopus commit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the upstream-doctor characterization (its default moves non-chosen bundles to new branches; deletion is opt-in via --delete-bundle, per the awslabs README/DeepWiki) and justify the bespoke module against that non-destructive mode — state precisely why driving upstream's branch-preserving path non-interactively + reusing rebar's _union_merge is insufficient, rather than relying on a 'discards events' claim that the retrieved upstream docs contradict.
evidence: Plan quote: 'it **discards** the non-chosen head — i.e. it *loses* every event unique to that head'

Retrieved awslabs/git-remote-s3 README (github.com): 'By default it will create a new branch for every bundle that should not be retained. The user can then checkout the branch locally and merge it to the original branch.'

Retrieved DeepWiki 'Management Tools' (deepwiki.com/awslabs/git-remote-s3/4-management-tools): 'asks the user which one to keep. The others are either moved to new branches (with generated names) or deleted based on the --delete-bundle flag.'

T1(a): directly-adjacent prior art (the very tool being replaced) is mischaracterized and its non-discard mode is not considered; T1(c): the load-bearing capability assertion 'the upstream doctor discards events' is unresolved against the retrieved upstream docs.
findings.finding: The plan's central motivation misstates the upstream git-remote-s3 doctor prior art: it claims the upstream doctor 'discards' / 'loses every event unique to that head', but the upstream README and awslabs/git-remote-s3 DeepWiki describe a non-destructive DEFAULT that moves non-chosen bundles to new branches (preserving them), with deletion only under an opt-in --delete-bundle flag. The plan does not consider or rebut this branch-preservation mode as adjacent prior art.
findings.location: Context/Problem paragraph 2 ('Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only ... and it **discards** the non-chosen head — i.e. it *loses* every event unique to that head')
scenarios: A reviewer/author later discovers upstream already preserves the non-chosen head as a branch and questions whether a from-scratch S3 heal module is warranted, or whether the far smaller delta is (a) invoke upstream doctor in its non-delete branch-preserving mode non-interactively, then (b) reuse rebar's existing _union_merge on the generated branches.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-anchor the motivation on the verifiable gaps (blocking input() at manage.py that crashes on EOF; no single-call autonomous convergence; requires a human to checkout+merge the generated branches afterward) and explicitly note that upstream's default is non-destructive but leaves the merge as a manual follow-up, which is what this story automates by feeding the divergent heads into rebar's existing _union_merge.

findings.finding: The heal mutates the local repo (fetch into scratch refs, then `git merge` to create T in base_path's worktree) but the plan specifies only the helper's S3 per-ref lock for serialization — it never says the local worktree mutation runs under rebar's own write_lock. sync.py deliberately runs its HEAD/index/worktree-mutating merge UNDER `write_lock` because a bare `git merge` races a concurrent local committer; the doctor omits that guard.
findings.location: Approach → Heal algorithm steps 3–4 and 7; Approach step 1 (locking)
